overrides.reason: Growth of FY2027 over the FY2026 guided 14.0bn. Base 26% (contracted): the order backlog was 15.0bn at 2025-12-31 (+109% y/y from 7.2bn, 'majority firm', shipping within 12-18 months) after Q4 2025 organic orders +252% and book-to-bill about 2.9x (trailing-twelve-month orders +81%); the FY2026 guide (14.0bn) less H1 (5.92bn) less the Q3 guide midpoint (3.75bn, organic +34-36%) implies Q4 2026 about 4.33bn (derived), i.e. an exit run rate of about 17.3bn, +24% over FY2026 before any sequential growth in 2027 (Q1 is seasonally lower: Q1 2026 2.65bn vs Q4 2025 2.88bn) and before a full year of the UIG acquisition (closed after the last balance sheet; its revenue is undisclosed, a gap). Bull 34% (contracted): orders keep the FY2025 pace so the backlog conversion of 12-18 months adds sequential growth through 2027 (about 18.8bn). Bear 6% (own history): the second half of the backlog ships but new orders stall after a hyperscaler/neocloud capex pause; Q2 2026 already came in 2.3% below the guided midpoint, large customers impose penalties and stricter terms (10-K), and 2026 orders and backlog are no longer disclosed, so a slowdown would not be visible in advance. Not consensus: the broad FY2027 revenue consensus is dated 2026-10-27 and not citable at as_of (cross-check in gaps only).

GAAP operating margin after SBC and acquired-intangible amortization. History: FY2023 12.7%, FY2024 17.1%, FY2025 17.9%, H1 2026 18.2% (Q1 16.6%, Q2 19.5%); the FY2026 guide (adjusted 23.3-24.3%, GAAP EPS 5.82-5.92 vs adjusted 6.65-6.75) implies a GAAP margin of roughly 21% for FY2026 with a heavier second half (Q3 adjusted guide 24-25%). Base 20%: above FY2025 because the gains were broad (every segment's margin rose in Q2 2026, including shrinking EMEA) and price-cost held, but below the FY2026 peak (quarter review flag peak_margin_run_rate) because Eaton, Schneider, Legrand and Delta are all adding data-center capacity. Bear 14%: between FY2023 (12.7%) and FY2024 (17.1%), the level before the AI-driven price-cost gains, as capacity catches up and price competition returns. Bull 23% (guidance): the guided Q3/FY2026 adjusted margin of 23-25% is held through the cycle and acquired-intangible amortization fades, so GAAP approaches adjusted.

Revenue added per dollar of net invested capital (equity + long-term debt - cash), net of customer advances (the engine funds growth capex + working capital - change in deferred revenue from this ratio). Base 3.5 = VRT's FY2023-25 record: revenue +3.37bn on invested capital +0.95bn (4.15bn -> 5.11bn), which already includes the PurgeRite purchase (Nov 2025). The earlier 2.2 counted acquisitions already paid for in the opening balance and, for UIG, deducted again as a 1.45bn debt-like claim (double count). Cross-check with the company's own capex: FY2023-25 capex 1.9-2.2% of revenue (128m, 167m, 220m) and the FY2026 guide 550-570m (~4% of 14.0bn); with working capital funded largely by advances (current deferred revenue 3.63bn at H1 2026), a capex-guide build implies an even higher ratio, so 3.5 is the conservative company figure. Bear 2.2 = FY2024 -> FY2025 (revenue +2.22bn on capital +0.99bn incl. PurgeRite): growth bought, advances unwind. Bull 4.0 (guidance-anchored): between the record and the FY2026 capex-guide build. Future acquisitions (UIG earnout up to 1.15bn) stay a gap, not a number.

Stock-based compensation as a share of revenue: FY2025 45.9m / 10.23bn = 0.45%, H1 2026 30.8m / 5.92bn = 0.52%; 0.5% in every scenario (the same plan in each; dilution of about +1% a year in diluted shares is carried in the share count).

Perpetual return on new capital after 2041, from VRT's own post-turnaround record (NOPAT = operating income x (1 - 24.7% normalized tax); invested capital = equity + long-term debt - cash, year end): FY2023 15.8% (872m x 0.753 / 4.15bn), FY2024 25.0% (1,367m x 0.753 / 4.11bn), FY2025 27.0% on year-end capital (1,830m x 0.753 / 5.11bn; 29.9% on average capital, the 30% the yearly path uses). Base 23% = the FY2023-25 average (22.6%): a fade from today's ~30% to the three-year through-cycle level, which was earned at an average GAAP margin of 15.9%, below the base terminal margin of 20%, so it is conservative for the base margin. Bear 16% = FY2023, the first post-turnaround year (margin 12.7%, near the bear 14%). Bull 30% = FY2025 on average capital (held). Why it differs from company_path: the path ROIC (bear 15% / base 30% / bull 43%) is the incremental return over the next five years at today's economics; the terminal ROIC is the level after Eaton, Schneider, Legrand and Delta add data-center capacity (mature_margin reason), so base fades 30% -> 23%. Replaces the engine moat rule (Ku + 50% of excess = 12.1%), which had no company data. No named-competitor ROIC was retrieved (gap), so no competitor level is used.

current_year_revenue.basis: FY2026 revenue: company guidance midpoint 14,000,000,000 (13,800,000,000-14,200,000,000, issued 2026-07-29); FY2026 revenue = the latest company guidance midpoint, 14.0bn (13.8-14.2bn, issued 2026-07-29, raised from 13.5bn in February and 13.75bn in April). Not adjusted by the 1.040 track-record ratio: the beats have narrowed (Q4 2025 1.011, FY2025 1.003, Q1 2026 1.019) and Q2 2026 missed the guided midpoint (0.977) on supply-chain congestion and project phasing, so a ratio near 1.00 is the honest reading for the unreported second half. The Q3 2026 results of 2026-10-28 are not citable until 2026-10-30.

cyclical.reason: Revenue has not fallen in any year since FY2020 (4.37bn -> 10.23bn) and the margin rose every year from FY2022 (3.9%) to FY2025 (17.9%) through the turnaround, price-cost and productivity, with gains in every segment in Q2 2026; the econ review finds no price-cyclical model. The cyclical element is the customers' capex (orders +252% in Q4 2025, book-to-bill 2.9x vs 1.2x in Q2 2025) and the FY2022 price-cost squeeze: carried in the bear scenario and the key risk, not in a mid-cycle margin anchored on the turnaround years.

debt_like_claims.reason: UIG (Utility Innovation Group) acquisition: 1.45bn of upfront cash under the merger agreement of 2026-09-01 (8-K 2026-09-02), payable after the last filed balance sheet (2026-06-30) from existing resources; the opening cash in the engine still holds it. The contingent part (up to 1.15bn) has no disclosed fair value and is left as a gap, not a number.

Contingent consideration liability for earlier acquisitions (PurgeRite and others) at fair value on the 2026-06-30 balance sheet (10-Q); payable in cash ahead of the shareholders and not in the debt lines.

bear.reason_he: בתרחיש הדובי ההון החדש מרוויח כ-15% בשנה: זה הממוצע של Vertiv בשנים 2020 עד 2025 (כ-14.4%), שכולל את שנות ההבראה שבהן הרווחיות הייתה 4%-5%. מה נשבר: המתחרים מוסיפים כושר ייצור, המחירים יורדים, והצמיחה נקנית ברכישות יקרות (UIG ב-1.45 מיליארד דולר ועד 1.15 מיליארד נוספים, PurgeRite ב-1.14 מיליארד) שהתשואה עליהן עוד לא הוכחה. תשואה כזו קרובה יותר למחיר ההון, ולכן המכפיל נמוך יותר.

base.reason_he: בתרחיש הבסיסי ההון החדש מרוויח כ-30% בשנה, כמו התשואה על ההון של Vertiv ב-2025 (30.4%, כולל מוניטין מרכישות). התשואה על ההון הנוסף בשנים 2023-2025 הייתה גבוהה יותר (כ-68%), אבל היא מנופחת במקדמות של לקוחות ובשנות שיא, וההון שהולך לרכישות מוריד אותה. 30% זה הרבה מעל מחיר ההון, ולכן מכפיל גבוה מוצדק, והוא יורד עם האטת הצמיחה.

bull.reason_he: בתרחיש השורי ההון החדש מרוויח כ-43% בשנה: זו התשואה על ההון שנוסף ל-Vertiv בין 2020 ל-2025 (הרווח התפעולי אחרי מס עלה הרבה יותר מההון). כדי שזה יקרה, הצמיחה צריכה להגיע ממפעלים קיימים שהוכפלו, המקדמות של הלקוחות צריכות להמשיך לממן את המלאי, והשוליים של 24-25% צריכים להישמר. זו תשואה של תקופת מחסור, לכן היא לא מוכחת לטווח ארוך.

own_history.years: 2023-04 to 2026-09 (42 months): TRAILING P/E = month-end close (IBKR) / TTM GAAP diluted EPS, months with TTM EPS < 0.30 excluded. Not a forward P/E (no dated consensus series exists): a forward multiple on growing EPS sits well below the trailing one (today 48.2x trailing on TTM 4.42 vs 36.3x on the FY2026 GAAP guide midpoint 5.87). 2024 GAAP EPS is depressed by warrant fair-value losses, inflating 2024 multiples; the post-2025 trailing range is 49.6-84.1 (median about 70).

bear.event_he: הלקוחות הגדולים (ענקיות הענן ו-neocloud כמו CoreWeave ו-Nebius, שהם 'חלק מהותי' מהלקוחות) עוצרים חלק מההשקעות ב-2027: ההזמנות נעצרות אחרי שהצבר הנוכחי נשלח, וההכנסות עולות רק כ-6%. אין דיווח על הזמנות וצבר מאז סוף 2025, ולכן האטה לא תיראה מראש.
המתחרים (Eaton, Schneider, Legrand, Delta) מוסיפים כושר ייצור ושוק הקירור הנוזלי מתמלא: המחירים יורדים והרווח התפעולי חוזר לכ-14% מהמכירות, כמו בין 2023 ל-2024.
ההחמצה של הרבעון השני של 2026 (3.27 מיליארד מול 3.35 בתחזית, בגלל עומס בשרשרת האספקה) חוזרת: הפרויקטים הגדולים נדחים והלקוחות גובים קנסות על איחורים.
הנתח באירופה ממשיך להישחק (מכירות EMEA ירדו 8.4% במחצית הראשונה של 2026 בזמן ש-Schneider ו-Legrand צמחו).

הרכישות (UIG ב-1.45 מיליארד דולר ועד 1.15 מיליארד נוספים לפי ביצועים, PurgeRite, King Environmental) לא מחזירות את המחיר, והתחייבויות התמורה המותנית (234.6 מיליון דולר, הפסד שווי של 62 מיליון במחצית) ממשיכות לגדול.
המקדמות של הלקוחות (1.8 מיליארד דולר נוספו לתזרים במחצית הראשונה של 2026) מתהפכות כשהפרויקטים נשלחים, והתזרים של 2027 נופל הרבה מתחת ל-2026.

base.event_he: 2026 נסגרת סביב 14.0 מיליארד דולר הכנסות, אמצע התחזית שהחברה העלתה שלוש פעמים השנה (13.5, 13.75, 14.0), בלי תוספת על בסיס ההיסטוריה כי ההפתעות לטובה הצטמצמו ורבעון 2 החמיץ.
ב-2027 ההכנסות עולות כ-26%: הצבר של 15 מיליארד דולר בסוף 2025 (פי 2 משנה קודם, רובו חתום, נשלח תוך 12-18 חודשים) וקצב של כ-4.3 מיליארד ברבעון הרביעי של 2026 כבר נותנים כ-17.3 מיליארד בשנה.
הרווח התפעולי מתייצב סביב 20% מהמכירות: מעל 17.9% של 2025 כי השיפור היה בכל האזורים, אבל מתחת לשיא של 2026 כי המתחרים מוסיפים כושר ייצור.
רכישת UIG (1.45 מיליארד דולר במזומן) הופכת את המזומן נטו הקטן (כ-171 מיליון דולר ביוני 2026) לחוב נטו, והצמיחה ממשיכה לכלול רכישות.
השירותים והחלפים (20% מהמכירות, +28.6% ברבעון השני) ממשיכים לגדול עם בסיס המערכות המותקן ומייצבים את הרווח.

bull.event_he: ההזמנות נשארות בקצב 2025 (עלייה של 81% בשנה, יחס הזמנות למכירות 2.9 ברבעון הרביעי): הצבר בסוף 2026 עולה מעל 15 מיליארד דולר וההכנסות של 2027 עולות כ-34%, לכ-18.8 מיליארד.
השוליים המתואמים של 24-25% שהחברה הנחתה לרבעון השלישי של 2026 נשמרים, וכשהפחתת הנכסים מרכישות נחלשת הרווח התפעולי החשבונאי מגיע לכ-23%.
Vertiv ממשיכה לצמוח מהר יותר מ-Eaton באמריקה (21% אורגני מול 18% ברבעון השני) ולוקחת את התוכן החדש של שרתי בינה מלאכותית: קירור נוזלי וחלוקת חשמל במתח גבוה.
כושר הייצור שהוכפל והשקעות של כ-4% מהמכירות ב-2026 משחררים את צוואר הבקבוק בשרשרת האספקה, והפרויקטים נשלחים בזמן.

bottleneck_potential.reading: VRT is today one of the bottlenecks of AI data-center build-outs: book-to-bill about 2.9x in Q4 2025, backlog above one year of sales, Q2 2026 sales held back by supply-chain congestion and project phasing, capacity more than doubled since 2021 and FY2026 capex raised to about 4% of revenue. It is a shared bottleneck, not a unique one: Eaton, Schneider, Legrand and Delta report the same demand and are adding capacity and buying liquid-cooling capability (Schneider-Motivair, Eaton-Boyd Thermal). The scarcity lasts while customer capex grows faster than the combined additions of these five suppliers; no dated balance is evidenced.

share_trajectory.reading: Mixed on numbers. Americas: VRT +21.1% organic in Q2 2026 vs Eaton Electrical Americas +18% organic (VRT slightly ahead; Eaton's segment includes non-data-center markets). Orders: VRT backlog +109% y/y at 2025-12-31 vs Eaton Electrical Americas backlog +33% at June 2026 (periods differ). Total growth: VRT +17.8% organic in Q2 2026 trailed Delta (revenue +48%) and Legrand's data-center business (>30% organic in H1). EMEA: VRT sales -8.4% in H1 2026 while Schneider grew +18.8% organic in Energy Management (Q3) and Legrand +9.8% organic group-wide: VRT is losing share in EMEA. No attributed market-share study was retrieved.

competitive_position.reading: Against Eaton: about equal (VRT Q2 2026 adjusted operating margin 22.6% vs Eaton Electrical Americas 27.5% and Electrical Global 19.8%; VRT grows slightly faster in the Americas; Eaton is far larger, 27.4bn of FY2025 revenue). Against Schneider: weaker in Europe (share loss) and in scale, comparable in data-center thermal now that Schneider owns Motivair. Against Legrand: stronger in power and thermal systems, Legrand stronger in white space (racks, PDUs) and with a similar margin (20.8% adjusted in H1). Against Delta: higher margin (VRT 22.6% adjusted vs Delta 16.7% operating) but Delta grows faster in AI rack power. Against JCI: VRT is the larger data-center thermal specialist; JCI grows +7.5% group-wide. Edge: the breadth of power plus thermal with a services base (20% of sales, +28.6%), not an exclusive technology.

threats.reading: 1) Competitor capacity: every named competitor is adding data-center capacity and liquid cooling, so a pause in customer capex would turn the backlog into price competition. 2) Customer bargaining power: the 10-K says large hyperscale/neocloud customers are a material portion of the base and impose penalties and stricter delivery terms; concentration is not disclosed. 3) Technology shift: higher rack density moves content to liquid cooling and higher-voltage power, the entry path that Schneider (Motivair), Eaton (Boyd Thermal) and Delta bought or built. 4) In-sourcing or direct design by hyperscalers: hypothesis-level here, no evidence retrieved. 5) Growth increasingly bought (UIG 1.45bn plus up to 1.15bn earnout; PurgeRite 1.14bn).

bottlenecks.reading: Demand for VRT's power and thermal equipment runs well ahead of its deliveries: Q4 2025 organic orders +~252% y/y, book-to-bill ~2.9x, backlog $15.0bn at 2025-12-31 (+109% y/y), more than 1x the 2026 sales guidance midpoint of $14.0bn. Q3 2026 organic sales guide 34-36%.

VRT is adding its own capacity: it more than doubled switchgear, busbar and integrated power manufacturing capacity since late 2021; 2026 capex guided to $550-570m (raised from $425-525m in the 10-K) vs $226.4m in 2025; Q2 2026 sales were held back by 'temporary supply chain congestion and multi-phased project execution'. The binding constraint is factory output and supply chain, not demand.

Paid pricing power in VRT's own numbers: Q2 2026 adjusted operating margin 22.6%, +410 bp y/y, attributed by the company to productivity and favorable price-cost including tariff countermeasures; Q3 2026 guide 24.0-25.0%.

The shortage is shared and competitors are also scaling: Eaton Electrical Global backlog +103% and Electrical Americas backlog +33% y/y at June 2026 with Electrical Americas margin 27.5%; Schneider reports triple-digit data-center demand growth and a record backlog in Q3 2026; Legrand data centers 32% of sales, organic >30% in H1 2026; Delta revenue +48% in Q2 2026 with data center >50% of revenue. Capacity is being added by every named supplier, so the scarcity premium is not VRT's alone.

Market direction: the IEA (Energy and AI, April 2025) projects global data-centre electricity demand to more than double to ~945 TWh by 2030 (from ~415 TWh in 2024), with AI-optimised data-centre demand more than quadrupling and data centres almost half of US electricity demand growth to 2030. Power and cooling equipment per MW scales with this build-out (search excerpt, not the report itself).

How long the shortage lasts: it lasts while hyperscaler/AI capex keeps growing faster than the combined capacity additions of VRT, Eaton, Schneider, Legrand and Delta; a capex pause or a catch-up of supplier capacity (all five are expanding) would turn backlog into price competition. No dated supply/demand balance from an attributed study was retrieved.

Rising rack power density (AI racks) shifts content toward liquid cooling and higher-voltage power distribution, where VRT, Schneider (Motivair), Eaton (Boyd Thermal) and Delta all compete; the technology shift is both VRT's opportunity and the entry path for competitors that bought liquid-cooling capacity in 2025-26.
